text:
ConocoPhillips rose 1.6% today to $142.28, continuing a five-day rally that's recovered most of last week's losses. The stock has gained $5.74 since November 6th, tracking closely with oil prices: US crude is now at $89.62 per barrel, up from the lows that triggered the earlier sell-off. The immediate bounce appears tied to stabilization in energy markets after recent volatility.

The broader context matters here: while Russian crude production has rebounded and global oil markets have shifted toward surplus according to recent IEA data, heating oil prices remain dramatically elevated—up 59% from last winter. This split between crude oversupply and tight refined product markets creates complexity for integrated energy companies like ConocoPhillips, which both produce crude and operate refining capacity. The recent rally suggests the market is focusing on production volumes and oil prices rather than concerns about refining margin compression.
